verification_report.summary:
Correct under the explicitly accepted prerequisite degenerate_nonuniqueness_01. The full prerequisite file was read, and the supplied proof was audited in textual order through 75 individual deductions in 15 statement-check records, followed by three reference-check records. No critical errors or gaps were found.

The strict half-excess gives the required opposite endpoint signs. Strict monotonicity supplies a unique J(I) for every I in a nondegenerate interval. Balance makes both slope joins continuous, and the derivative inequalities correctly give -p <= h <= p. The exact cutoff supports make the left Q coefficient and right P coefficient vanish; the middle R coefficient vanishes. All remaining coefficients are nonnegative with the fixed book convention for ddc.

The primitives extend globally as C1,1 functions: the nonconstant band is compactly contained in U, and each projective end has a constant extension. Matching first derivatives exclude hypersurface terms in the weak Hessian. Local convolution gives uniformly bounded Hessians converging strongly in every finite L^s, hence Hessian products converge in L^1. Bedford--Taylor uniform continuity identifies these products; expanding with smooth forms handles the nonclosed background. Thus the Monge--Ampere measure has no extra transition-surface mass and equals exactly the prescribed f omega_X^3.

Distinct switch parameters give unequal slopes on an open interval, so neither subtracting rho nor supremum normalization identifies them. Each new solution also differs from both original smooth solutions. The unique symmetric root supplies an admissible pair; its slope is odd and its primitive even. With the permitted even cutoff for rho, the normalized potential and the exact equation data are invariant under block exchange. This pair is covered by the construction for all admissible pairs, regardless of the smaller interval used to establish uncountability.

The permitted Bedford--Taylor input was corroborated by arXiv-first lookup and direct inspection of [Theorem 4.1, equation (6)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1301.1796), with its continuous-limit hypotheses checked. No new PDE theorem, averaging argument, novelty claim, or approximation-convergence assertion is used. The full readable audit is saved in [verification_report.md](/Users/mingchen/Non-Kahler/research/rethlas/verification/results/numa_radial_family_01/verification_report.md); all checks are persisted in this run's verification memory.
